reason: The mechanism is right and the consequence, which is the only part that would earn a change at this bar, is wrong twice over. Driven in chromium at 1440 on ?v=light&state=full with the oldest mark focused, Accessibility.getFullAXTree does show StaticText "41 days open" and StaticText "Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company" at ignored:false, and a role "deletion" node for the - role="presentation" on #tip:543 strips only the div's own role, exactly as the seat says. But walk the parent chain rather than the flat node list: the tip div is itself dropped, and its and are reparented onto body as its LAST two children, after the node that holds banner, main and contentinfo. The strings therefore land at the very end of the document, past the footer, not beside the mark. Focusing a mark announces the button's aria-label and nothing more; the tip is filled by fill() at :1084 as a plain innerHTML write into a non-live, unreferenced element (nothing carries aria-describedby to #tip), and no reader speaks an arbitrary DOM mutation outside a live region. So no user 'meets each job's title twice while it holds focus'. Second: the tip never holds nine jobs, it holds one. hide() and drop() at :1094-1095 only remove the .on class - measured after Escape, innerHTML is still 41 days openConfirm the marquee sides... - so what a browse-mode cursor actually finds at the document end is ONE stale title, whichever mark was shown last, and before any hover it is empty. Third, the implication is asserted, not measured: text-decoration is none at :386 and announcement of deletion semantics is an off-by-default per-reader setting, so 'marked up as struck-out content' is not established as something a reader hears. The fix's numbers are also wrong in two of three places: the is authored at :783 inside strip()'s data-tip, not at :1085 (:1084 is fill, :1085 is place), and the two rules are at :386-387, not :382-383. What survives is a stray, stale, orphaned string at the end of the tree - real, one attribute wide, and correctly classed refinement, meaning nothing is wrong. It does not move this engagement.
sharpenedFix: If it is swept up with other tidying, the whole of it is one attribute: add aria-hidden="true" to #tip at lately.html:543. The tip has zero focusable descendants (measured: #tip a,button,input,[tabindex] returns 0), is pointer-events:none, and every string it prints already exists verbatim in each mark's aria-label at :783, so the subtree can leave the tree with nothing lost. That alone removes the <s>/deletion node too, which makes the second half of the proposed fix optional; if the markup is changed anyway for its own sake, the <s> to re-key is the one authored at :783, and the rules are .tip s at :386 and [data-v="dark"] .tip s at :387 - not :382-383. Do not instead clear innerHTML on hide(): that would re-parse the tip's markup on every dismiss and reintroduce the work fill()/place() were split apart at :1083-1084 to avoid.
breaks: aria-hidden on #tip breaks nothing in the behaviour gate: interaction-check.mjs reads the tip through classList and textContent at :439-443, :456-460, :469, :474, :483, :487 and :1195-1199, none of which aria-hidden touches, and the stale-tip-strands-on-scroll guard at :1184 is likewise class-based. If the <s> is also re-keyed to a span, re-measure the tip's second line for colour and leading in both grounds - .tip s at :386-387 is the only place --mark-ctx and --ink-4 are applied to it, so a missed rule leaves that line at inherited paper-white in light and drops the dark override, which is a contrast regression the audit gate would have to catch against the fixed #111111 tip backdrop. Also re-run the audit for the type ramp: the rule sets font-size 13px / var(--lead-body) explicitly, so the ramp classification of the new selector must land where .tip s did.
